title: Go in Peace! — Serene Dismission
description: Go in Peace! — Serene Dismission in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 64, “Go in Peace”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7) (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Go in peace! se-rene dis-mis-sion To the lov-ing heart made known, When it pours in deep con-tri-tion Prayer be-fore th'e-ter-nal throne.

lines: To the loving heart made known,
When it pours in deep contrition
Go in peace! thy sins forgiven,
Christ hath healed thee, set thee free
O'er our spirits while we pray;
Let us part in sweet conviction
Thou hast blessed our souls to-day.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
